method: Step 6 direct project-level research fallback, extended window per Asif's completeness question -- the 6-month pass (il-sangamon-research-fallback.json) was checked for completeness two ways: (1) an agenda/primary-record-focused re-query (found no new qualifying projects, but its own docket-number citations could not be independently verified -- no real URL locatable for Ordinance 2026-223 or Zoning Docket #2026-016), (2) this 3-year window extension, which DID surface 3 genuinely new projects the 6-month window missed because their dated action fell outside it.
cross_check_summary: 8 unique projects total (5 from the original 6-month/broader pass + 3 new from the 3-year extension: UIS Innovation Center, Springfield Clinic Pediatrics Center, Abraham Lincoln Capital Airport terminal/hangar expansion). All 3 new projects' facts independently cross-checked and CONFIRMED (cost, SF, contractor/architect, dates all held up on a fresh search). One more fabricated document URL caught in the same round: UIS Innovation Center's claimed Board of Trustees PDF (bot.uillinois.edu/.../2023-09-21-026.pdf) is a 404 -- flyspi.com (cited for the airport RFP) is a real domain but the specific claimed document was not independently verified as pullable.
load_status: NOT LOADED -- verified findings only, load path not yet built.
completeness_note: This confirms time-window choice has a real recall cost: the 6-month window was not just narrower by design, it silently dropped 3 legitimate projects whose only dated action (approval, groundbreaking, completion) happened to fall before the window start. A 6-month 'recent activity' view and a 'currently relevant to reps' view are not the same thing -- a project completed in 2023 may still be worth having in the corpus even though it has no 2026 dated action.
